manifest.research_question: Research verified literature where user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry and generative semantic IDs intersect.

sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
sources.exact_overlap: Directly covers user next-item behavior and generative semantic IDs: a Transformer sequence-to-sequence model predicts the Semantic ID for the next item from a user's chronologically ordered interaction history. Full text describes content embeddings quantized into residual-quantized codeword tuples (RQ-VAE) and the next-item training objective (Sections 3.1–3.2). It does not use or report hyperbolic geometry; semantic hierarchy is learned with RQ-VAE, not a demonstrated hyperbolic manifold.
sources.verification_note: Inspected the arXiv HTML full text, not merely the abstract. The abstract explicitly states the next-item Semantic ID prediction task; Sections 3.1–3.2 detail the representation and training setup.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Mamba for Sequential Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Overlaps user sequential behavior and hyperbolic geometry: abstract says sequential recommendation models temporal evolution of user preferences from interaction sequences and proposes Hyperbolic Mamba to represent hierarchy-aware sequence dynamics. The inspected abstract does not establish generative retrieval or generative semantic IDs.
sources.verification_note: arXiv search result/abstract text verified; full text was not inspected for this report.

sources.title: Poincaré Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks for Sequential Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Overlaps sequential user preference/behavior and hyperbolic geometry: abstract describes sequential recommendation, user-item interaction hierarchies, and Poincaré-space graph representations with temporal attention. The inspected abstract does not mention generative recommendation or semantic IDs.
sources.verification_note: arXiv search result/abstract text verified; full text was not inspected for this report.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Hypergraphs for Sequential Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Overlaps sequential user-item interaction behavior and hyperbolic geometry: abstract presents H2SeqRec, using hyperbolic hypergraph convolution and temporal/hierarchical item representations for sequential recommendation. The inspected abstract does not establish generative semantic IDs.
sources.verification_note: arXiv search result/abstract text verified; full text was not inspected for this report.

sources.title: HCGR: Hyperbolic Contrastive Graph Representation Learning for Session-based Recommendation
sources.exact_overlap: Overlaps session-based user behavior and hyperbolic geometry: abstract says it models user preferences from behavior sequences using Lorentz hyperbolic representations and adaptive hyperbolic attention. The inspected abstract does not establish generative retrieval or semantic IDs.
sources.verification_note: arXiv search result/abstract text verified; full text was not inspected for this report.

sources.title: HypRQ-VAE: Hyperbolic Item Indexing for Long-Tail-Aware Generative Recommender Systems
sources.exact_overlap: The abstract describes hyperbolic item indexing for generative recommendation, encoding item semantics and long-tail structure in hyperbolic space. It is a very close hyperbolic-plus-generative-indexing match, but the inspected abstract does not specifically establish user next-item behavioral conditioning or confirm that its generated index is the same Semantic ID formulation used by TIGER. Treat as a promising near-match, not verified complete three-way overlap.
sources.verification_note: arXiv search result/abstract text verified. This work was announced September 2026, before the frozen report date (2026-10-24). Full text was not inspected.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Behavior-first next-item modeling with hyperbolic state/sequence representations and generative semantic-ID decoding
behavior_problem_candidates.basis: TIGER (FULL_TEXT) provides an explicit behavioral target and semantic-ID decoder; HMamba and the listed hyperbolic sequential/session papers (ABSTRACT) provide evidence that hyperbolic representations are used for sequential preference or interaction behavior. HypRQ-VAE (ABSTRACT) suggests a current bridge between hyperbolic item indexing and generative recommendation.
behavior_problem_candidates.overlap_status: No independently verified source inspected here demonstrates all three elements together: user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry, and generative semantic IDs.
behavior_problem_candidates.testable_question: Does replacing Euclidean item semantic-ID quantization and/or the sequence state space with a hyperbolic hierarchy improve next-item ranking and tail-item generalization, compared with TIGER-style Euclidean RQ-VAE semantic IDs and hyperbolic sequential baselines?
behavior_problem_candidates.behavioral_evaluation: Evaluate next-item Recall/NDCG or MRR, separately reporting head/tail and cold-start items; compare against both a generative-SID baseline and hyperbolic sequential baseline. Avoid claiming behavior improvement from geometric fit alone.

limitations: No verified full-text paper in this search directly establishes the complete three-way intersection. The strongest evidence is complementary: TIGER directly verifies next-item behavior plus generative semantic IDs, while the hyperbolic sequential papers verify the geometry/behavior side only at abstract level.

FULL_TEXT means an arXiv HTML full-text page was opened and relevant sections inspected; ABSTRACT means only arXiv abstract/search-result text was inspected. A listed PDF/full-text URL is a locator, not evidence that its content was read.

HypRQ-VAE appears highly relevant but abstract-level evidence alone does not establish next-item conditioning or a precise equivalence between its item index and TIGER-style semantic IDs. Verify its full text before asserting the full overlap.
The source set is a targeted intersection search, not a systematic review; absence of a full three-way match here is not proof that none exists.
No prior-candidate prompts, unseen future interactions, or test interactions were used.
